dimension_1.justification: The specification covers all explicit requirements (brief creation, budget, eligibility, marketplace discovery) and thoroughly derives implicit lifecycle requirements, including draft editing, pause/resume, soft-deletion/archiving, and automated Celery expiration (US-001 through US-009). It details full CRUD capabilities, dual-persona flows for Brands and Creators (such as pre-application eligibility evaluations in US-006), and a 6-state lifecycle with 10 explicit transitions and guard validations. No functional gaps exist relative to the requested 4-week production-ready scope.

dimension_2.justification: The document defines 9 robust edge cases (EC-001 to EC-009) covering concurrency, TOCTOU state changes, decimal floating-point precision, cache stampedes, cross-service identity deactivation, unsynced profile metrics, XSS injection, idempotency, and timezone normalization. Each edge case specifies both an architectural handling strategy and an exact technical mitigation (e.g., OCC versioning via SQLAlchemy, Redis idempotency caching, and Bleach sanitization). Furthermore, individual user stories include granular negative and boundary acceptance criteria (e.g., AC-002-2, AC-003-2, AC-004-3).

dimension_3.justification: The agent identifies 6 high-impact, non-obvious ambiguities (CQ-001 through CQ-006) addressing essential architectural concerns, including escrow vs. non-custodial ledger obligations, service boundary splits with Content Service for application intake, and post-publish mutability rules. Each question clearly analyzes both business and technical impacts, identifies the validation stakeholder, and defines a sensible, production-oriented default assumption for the 4-week V1 launch.

dimension_4.justification: The specification demonstrates exemplary structural hygiene, organizing requirements into uniquely identifiable user stories (US-001 to US-009) with Gherkin-style Given/When/Then acceptance criteria tagged by scenario type. Requirements are atomic, testable, and mapped to a MoSCoW prioritization matrix aligned with sprint delivery milestones (P0 through P2). The specification is further enhanced by complete REST API contracts and PostgreSQL schema definitions.

dimension_5.justification: Comprehensive, quantified non-functional requirements are provided across performance (e.g., P95 < 100ms marketplace browse under 1,000 RPS), security (RS256 JWT validation, tenant-scoped authorization, rate limiting), data integrity (NUMERIC types, OCC, audit trails), resilience (graceful degradation, Celery DLQs), and observability (Prometheus and OpenTelemetry). All architectural decisions directly leverage and respect the prescribed tech stack (FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery) within a realistic 4-week timeline.

scores.overall_assessment: This specification is an exemplary, production-grade requirements and architecture document that translates an ambiguous product request into an exceptionally structured, testable, and feasible implementation plan. It excels in domain boundary definition, state machine formalization, concurrency handling, and pragmatic MVP scoping.

dimension_5.justification: The spec provides concrete, quantitative non-functional requirements including p95/p99 latency SLAs, peak throughput targets, JWT-based tenant RBAC, PII data masking, and Redis sliding-window rate limits.
